ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The basic structure of the electric pickup in an electric guitar is shown in Figure 12. The metal strings near the magnet are magnetized, so when the strings vibrate, an induced current is produced in the coil. After the current is amplified by the circuit, it is transmitted to the speaker to produce sound. Which of the following statements are correct? (　　)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The basic structure of the electric pickup in an electric guitar is shown in Figure 12. If the magnet is removed, can the electric guitar still work normally?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an electric guitar, and the position of the pickup is drawn out and enlarged; in the enlarged view, a "metal string" is labeled above, and near the metal string there is a "magnet" labeled with N and S poles. A "coil" is wound around the magnet, and the two ends of the coil are connected to the output end "to the amplifier." Reasoning: The normal operation of the electric pickup depends on the magnet providing a magnetic field and causing the metal string to be magnetized; when the metal string vibrates, it causes the magnetic flux passing through the coil to change, thereby producing an induced current in the coil, which is then sent to the amplifier. If the magnet is removed, there is no stable source of magnetic field, and the metal string also cannot be effectively magnetized, so a normal induced signal cannot be produced in the coil. Therefore, the electric guitar cannot work normally. Final answer: It cannot work normally.
